sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Die-Struck Brass Cloisonné Polishing of Novelty Enamel Badges

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Agreement (DTA signed 1 April 1996, amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-People's Republic of China DTA (signed 15 March 1995, in force 1996)
Luxembourg-France DTA (signed 1 April 1958, amended by the 24 November 2006 Avenant)
Luxembourg-Germany DTA (signed 23 August 1958, amended by the 11 December 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom DTA (Convention of 24 May 1967, as amended)
EU-level investment protection agreements applicable to Luxembourg (e.g., CETA, EU-Singapore IPA, EU-Vietnam IPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended to incorporate EU Directive 2015/849 and EU Directive 2018/843 and FATF standards; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 January 2019 on the RBE; amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT as amended; CRF (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) guidance on customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of passport or national identity certificate of each proposed manager and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or civil registry authority of the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) where the issuing state is a contracting party; otherwise consular legalization by the competent Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal records / police clearance certificate for each proposed manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by translation into French or German by a Luxembourg sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or banking reference letter dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution of the holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy in the country of origin plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing, incumbency and UBO registry extract of any corporate shareholder where the ultimate owner is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or competent registry authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with authenticated English, French or German translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and banking history for the share capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depositing Luxembourg credit institution or foreign correspondent bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued directly to the Luxembourg notary; apostille or consular legalization required only for foreign-issued originals

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ex-ante screening of all UBOs, proposed managers and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (including Council Regulations 2580/2001 and 881/2002 and all EU autonomous sanctions regimes), the U.S. OFAC SDN and 13599 lists where USD payment rails or correspondent clearing apply, and the Luxembourg administrative freezing measures; PEP identification is performed on the FATF standard as transposed by Article 3(7) of the 2004 AML Law, covering legislative, executive, judicial and military functions, plus family members and close associates; negative-news and adverse-media checks follow CSSF/CRF typologies; screening must be refreshed before execution of the notarial deed and at each material ownership change, with the results documented in the notary's CDD file for review by the CSSF and the CRF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), at lbr.lu, with the pre-incorporation name reservation performed through the LBR/RCS e-services and coordinated with the selected Luxembourg notary via guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; statutory filings are made in French or German (Luxembourgish is an official language but is not customary for RCS registration records); any non-Latin name element must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must include the legal form suffix 'SARL' or 'Societe a responsabilite limitee', must not conflict with an existing RCS booking, must not be contrary to public order or morality, and must not mislead the public as to the company's activity, legal form or affiliation, all pursuant to the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce where the name implies official chamber status
Societe Cooperative or SA where inconsistent with the SARL legal form
Luxembourg-only geographic tokens where the name falsely suggests state sponsorship
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the LBR/RCS registrar issues a reasoned refusal; the applicant may file a first-level re-examination request within one month through the LBR secured portal together with corrective evidence, such as a written consent from the conflicting name holder or a prior ministerial authorization for sensitive tokens. If the second decision remains adverse, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Tribunal administratif in Luxembourg City within three months of notification under the amended Law of 21 June 1999; objections relating to registry entries may be brought before the district court sitting in commercial matters. Parallel reservation of one to three backup names at the time of the notarial mandate is recommended to avoid expiry of the statutory validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the ISIC 3240 e-commerce activity subject to conditions: Luxembourg law requires a real and effective registered office in Luxembourg capable of receiving legal process; a virtual office or domiciliation arrangement is acceptable only where provided by a licensed domiciliation agent authorized under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended, and supervised where applicable by the CSSF; the arrangement must permit service of process, mail handling and inspection access, and must be disclosed to the notary and the RCS. A pure letterbox structure without any administrative capacity is likely to impair bank account opening, VAT registration and tax substance review for the enamel pins activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this industry tier: estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first operational year is below 5% for a compliant, standard-risk ISIC 3240 entity with a clean CDD file; the probability rises to approximately 20% to 35% where the CRF receives a suspicious transaction report, the tax administration opens a substance enquiry, or the domiciliation agent becomes subject to a CSSF thematic inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of the articles of association for the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff scaled to share capital; prevailing market benchmark EUR 2,000-2,800 plus disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 deposited on the SARL's blocked bank account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution holding the blockage certificate for the notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Minimum capital requirement under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; funds remain corporate assets and are not a fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank blockage certificate issuance fee for the share capital deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank tariff for a capital blockage attestation, EUR 100-300
Statutory LBR fee schedule of EUR 85 for registration of a legal person

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RESA electronic publication of the deed of incorporation and the articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff of approximately EUR 50-70 per notice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 180-183 and 189-5 (formation of SARL, minimum share capital, liberation of contributions, in-kind contribution audit).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts) executed by notarial deed (acte notarié) and the RCS registration file (formulaire d'immatriculation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000; at least one-fifth of the legal minimum (EUR 2,400) must be paid up in cash at incorporation into a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution, and any amount subscribed in excess of the EUR 12,000 minimum must be fully liberated; the balance of the minimum may be paid up within five years from RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a valuation report by a statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the subscription of one hundred shares of share capital, as set forth in the notarial deed of incorporation, is ratified and confirmed.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office designated in the Articles of Association is adopted as the principal place of business for all legal, tax and administrative purposes.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed as gérants, serving indefinitely until resignation or removal, and that the statutory-representative gérant is authorized to complete all registrations, including RCS, VAT, business licensing and social security filings.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the bank certificate evidencing the blocked capital contribution is approved and filed with the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation deposit of share capital into a blocked bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (commercial bank or CSSF-licensed payment institution) where the blocked account is opened in the name of the company in formation (société en formation).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder(s) sign the bank account opening forms and deposit at least EUR 2,400 (or the full paid-up portion if higher) in cash. The bank issues a certificate of blocked funds (attestation de blocage de fonds) addressed to the notary, stating the account holder, the deposited amount, and the irrevocable block until production of the RCS registration certificate. The certificate must be dated within two banking days of deposit and remain valid until the deed is signed.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Passport or national ID of each shareholder
Proof of residential address of each shareholder
AML/KYC forms: source of funds declaration and beneficial ownership statement
Bank account opening application and signature card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account or imposes enhanced due diligence, the founder may apply to another Luxembourg credit institution or request a reasoned AML waiver; a defective certificate is re-issued by the bank within two banking days upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire) practicing in the judicial arrondissement of Luxembourg or Diekirch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The shareholders (or their attorneys-in-fact) appear before the notary, who verifies identity, capacity, legality of the object, and the authenticity of the bank deposit certificate. The notary reads the articles, records shareholder consent, authenticates the deed, and delivers certified copies (expéditions). The gérants accept office at this moment. A notarial deed is mandatory for multi-member SARLs and is recommended over the private-deed route for bank and customer due diligence.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate (attestation bancaire de blocage de fonds)
Final draft of the Articles of Association
Valid passports/IDs and original notarized powers of attorney for corporate founders
Tax clearance certificate (certificat de non-faillite) for any corporate founding shareholder
Lease agreement or domiciliation certificate for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in the draft or in the supporting documents, a rectifying deed (acte rectificatif) is executed before the same notary; missing tax clearance certificates are obtained from the AEDT within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operational arm Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), filed via the LBR e-portal or the RCS counter at the Luxembourg District Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the notarial deed, the notary or an authorized representative submits the online registration file, pays the registration fee, and uploads the electronic copy of the deed, the statement of legal representatives, and proof of registered office. The RCS verifies the file and, upon approval, issues the company's registration number (matricule) and the European Company Number (ECN).
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (original or certified copy)
Form A - Statement of appointment of legal representatives and signatory powers
Proof of registered office (lease contract or domiciliation agreement)
Bank certificate evidencing paid-up capital
Valid identification documents and extracts (casier judiciaire) for each gérant
Payment receipt of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RCS queries must be answered within fifteen days; the applicant files a written explanatory memorandum with corrected forms or a supplemental notarial statement. If the application is rejected, the full dossier may be resubmitted within one month with cured deficiencies and an additional administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), the official electronic gazette operated under the authority of the Ministry of Justice and managed by LBR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary or LBR transmits the deed extract to the RESA within fifteen days. The publication discloses the corporate name, legal form, registered office, corporate object, subscribed and paid-up capital, and the identity and powers of the gérants. Third-party opposability of the deed and of the appointments commences on the date of RESA publication.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extract)
Copy of the notarial deed for publication
Publication fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or technically rejected, the company contacts the RESA helpdesk and resubmits the extract. Any publication errors are corrected through a supplementary announcement at the company's cost; legal opposability runs from the corrected publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration operational registrations and business establishment licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique (Single Contact Point) of the Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Association d'assurance accident (AAA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The statutory representative applies for the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) for the industrial manufacture of metal badges and enamel articles; simultaneously, the company registers for VAT with the AEDT (VAT number issued within fifteen days and retroactive to incorporation), files the employer declaration with the CCSS for the gérant and any employees, and subscribes occupational accident insurance with the AAA. All filings are made electronically via the Guichet unique with Luxtrust authentication.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt (registration extranet copy)
Business establishment license application form (DCE) filed via the Guichet unique
Valid ID and proof of residence of the gérant; work permit for third-country nationals
Lease agreement or ownership deed for the industrial premises
Articles of association and gérant mandate (power of representation)
VAT registration form and proof of the company's bank account
Employer registration declaration to the CCSS and accident insurance declaration to the AAA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Refusal of the business establishment license may be administratively appealed to the Minister of the Economy within three months; an incomplete VAT file is cured by resubmission with corrected Luxtrust signatures within five days; the company may file a provisional operation notice with the Guichet to avoid penalties while the license is pending.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des PME), acting through the Guichet unique (Single Contact Point).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) for the craft-industrial activity of manufacturing die-struck metal badges and hard enamel novelty articles, issued under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on the exercise of commercial, craft and industrial professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency), attached to the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment (installation classée) subject to registration/notification (Class 4) under the amended Law of 9 May 2014 on waste prevention and management and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 2 March 2015 on the classification of installations classées, covering surface treatment and enameling of non-ferrous metals; a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Law of 15 May 2018 and an Annex II EIA screening notice are not triggered for micro-scale badge workshops below the applicable surface area and solvent consumption thresholds, but a screening confirmation should be obtained from the Administration de l'Environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from degreasing, rinsing and polishing lines must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 December 2015: COD not exceeding 125 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 35 mg/L, lead not exceeding 0.5 mg/L, copper not exceeding 1.0 mg/L, and zinc not exceeding 3.0 mg/L; VOC emissions from enamel firing ovens must comply with the technical annexes of Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) for surface treatment activities; lead-based and cadmium-based enamel frits must be replaced with lead-free equivalents where technically and economically feasible; all residues are classified and disposed of under Regulation (EU) No 1357/2014 and the national waste management plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) and the municipal fire inspection service, covering the enamel kilns, solvent storage cabinets and extraction hoods; structural load inspection by an approved technical control office (e.g., Luxcontrol, Socotec) for presses, kilns and storage mezzanines; occupational health and safety clearance by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines - ITM) including the statutory risk assessment (évaluation des risques), noise and dust exposure monitoring, machine-guarding certificates, ventilation and fume extraction verification, lead/cadmium occupational exposure limits, and emergency evacuation planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg City (direct taxes: corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) (VAT and registration duties); Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCS) at lbr.lu for statutory incorporation and foreign-branch registration; unified e-filing portal via myguichet.lu and eCDF (Electronic Customs and Fiscal Documentation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SARL by notarial deed and file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS), which automatically triggers attribution of the national identification number (matricule/NIF) used as the tax identification number. 2. Register for VAT with the AED by filing Form 1 TVA online at guichet.lu before the first taxable transaction; no turnover threshold applies to a SARL exporter, and the VAT registration number (numero de TVA) is issued immediately. 3. File Form 1 (declaration de debut) for direct taxes (CIT, municipal business tax, net wealth tax) with the ACD within 15 days of commencement; no re-registration is needed because the matricule serves as the unified TIN. 4. For a non-resident entity establishing a Luxembourg branch or permanent establishment, deliver notarised, legalised constitutional documents to the RCS, appoint a Luxembourg authorised tax representative, and obtain a local matricule in the same manner. 5. Maintain all registration certificates and RCS extracts in the fiscal file; update the VAT registration with AED within 15 days of any change in activity, address, or legal form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the SARL (Societe a Responsabilite Limitee) is an opaque capital company resident in Luxembourg (seat or central administration in Luxembourg) and is fully taxable at entity level on worldwide income under Articles 159-164 LIR. It is subject to corporate income tax (IRC: 15% on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profit, 17% above, plus a 7% solidarity surcharge), municipal business tax (impot commercial communal, municipality-dependent rate), and net wealth tax (impot sur la fortune, 0.5%). No pass-through or tax-transparent status is available for a SARL; profits are taxed at entity level, and distributions may benefit from the participation exemption where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime: entity classification follows the statutory legal form registered with the RCS, and a SARL is always opaque for Luxembourg tax purposes. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal unity / group consolidation under Article 164bis LIR (irrevocable 5-year election, horizontal group possible); (ii) VAT grouping under Article 60 LTVT (authorisation of the AED, requiring a relationship of financial, economic and organisational interdependence); (iii) participation exemption under Article 166 LIR (election to exempt qualifying dividends and capital gains, holding of at least 10% or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million and a 12-month holding/commitment period); (iv) merger and cross-border restructuring relief under EU Directive 90/434/EEC as implemented. Hybrid mismatch exploitation is restricted by the ATAD implementing law of 25 February 2021: no hybrid entity election is available, and mismatched deductions are denied or correspondingly included where a hybrid instrument or hybrid transfer gives rise to a deduction/no-inclusion outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutee) governed by the Loi du 12 fevrier 1979 (LTVT) and transposed EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administrated by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold for resident taxable persons: every SARL making a taxable supply must register from its first transaction. Small business exemption under Article 57 LTVT applies only up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover and does not apply to exporters or to a SARL electing normal taxation. Distance sales of goods / imports of low-value consignments (<= EUR 150) benefit from the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold. Non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg have no threshold and must register (or use the OSS scheme).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance system, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based clearance for B2B invoices is in force. E-invoicing is mandatory only for B2G (public procurement) transactions, which must be transmitted through the PEPPOL e-invoicing network. For B2B transactions, e-invoicing is permitted subject to recipient consent; paper invoices remain valid. All VAT invoices must contain the statutory particulars under Article 50 LTVT, and the SARL must preserve original invoice files and audit trails for at least 6 years. Submission of periodic return and European Sales Lists is made via the AED's electronic portal (myguichet.lu / eCDF) with Intrastat filings where intra-EU goods movement thresholds are exceeded.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Article 40 LTVT to the export of goods where the SARL proves that the goods have physically left the EU customs territory; such exports are taxable at 0% VAT with full deduction of input VAT. Intra-community supplies to a taxable person holding a valid EU VAT number are exempt under Article 43 LTVT. Offshore/related services qualifying under Article 44 LTVT (services directly linked to exported goods, or services to a non-EU recipient with effective use and enjoyment outside the EU) may be zero-rated. The enamel-pin exporter must present at the time of the transaction conclusive evidence of the transport (commercial invoice, packing list, CMR/air waybill, bill of lading) and a written export declaration accepted by the customs office of exit. The exemption is denied where the supplier knew or ought to have known that the goods would not leave the EU (CJEU jurisprudence on the 'good faith' requirement and unlawful-abuse doctrine).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD, DEB, or Exit Summary Declaration) bearing the acceptance stamp of the customs office of exit (AES validation for EU export);
Commercial invoice and export packing list, endorsed with the customer and freight forwarder, showing the value, quantity and shipping terms (Incoterms 2020);
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Air Waybill / CMR road waybill, evidencing actual and unconditional physical movement of the goods out of the EU customs territory;
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/payment institution transfer record showing receipt of foreign currency settlement from the non-EU buyer;
Contract, purchase order, and any customs broker or freight forwarder instruction files supporting the export movement;
Intrastat declaration recapitulative statement (if the supply is intra-community, in respect of periodical EU transfers).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED and ACD conduct ex-post documentary audits of zero-rated exports and may require the SARL to produce all transport and payment evidence within a 30-day response period. Under Article 65 LTVT, false declarations, falsified documents, or fraudulent claims of zero-rating attract criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, and additional administrative penalties of up to 20% of the tax evaded. Regularisation of an unjustified zero-rating triggers immediate VAT repayment with interest and a retrospective reassessment window of up to 10 years in case of fraud (general rules of tax procedure). The AED may claw back the full input VAT claimed and disallow the deduction for related expenses, and the directors may be held jointly and severally liable; if the fraud involves EU-wide organised evasion, the matter is referred to OLAF with risk of cross-border customs proceedings and exclusion from public procurement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); exchange controls are integrated within the euro-area framework of the European Central Bank (ECB)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full capital and current account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions and the euro-area single currency system. No general exchange control authorization is required for foreign direct investment, loan repayment, or profit remittance. Dividends, branch profits, interest, royalties, and service income may be freely repatriated to non-resident shareholders and creditors, subject only to standard corporate tax, withholding tax, and beneficial ownership documentation requirements. For an enamel pin trading SARL, no administrative approval is required for the conversion of EUR into USD or other currencies for commercial transactions; banks merely require a valid underlying transaction document under their internal anti-money-laundering (AML) and sanctions protocols.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no timing deadlines under Luxembourg law. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in a foreign-currency account indefinitely or converted to EUR at the discretion of the SARL. For balance-of-payment statistical reporting, the BCL may require direct or bank-mediated data reporting for cross-border transactions exceeding certain thresholds, but this is a statistical obligation, not a surrender or conversion mandate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — Luxembourg-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed by the CSSF under the PSD2 regime, as well as EU/EEA EMIs passporting into Luxembourg, may offer streamlined online merchant accounts and virtual IBANs for low-risk e-commerce receivables. Cross-border digital EMIs domiciled outside the EU/EEA generally cannot operate in Luxembourg without obtaining a Luxembourg EMI license or an EU passport; fully offshore non-EU digital banks and payment processors are not viable as primary clearing rails due to CSSF restrictions on unlicensed deposit-taking and payment services. A regulated EMI can serve as an operational layer for Etsy and Stripe settlement acceleration, but the SARL should maintain at least one full-service Luxembourg commercial bank account for capital escrow, tax payments, and high-value trade settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is not an absolute statutory requirement in Luxembourg, but the account-opening bank and the CSSF expect that the director, the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and the mandate holder are reliably identified. Major banks in Luxembourg generally permit remote onboarding through digital KYC and a video interview when the natural persons already hold an EU passport, a Luxembourg residence permit, or an equivalent high-confidence digital identity. For a SARL with non-EU or complex shareholding structure, banks impose a mandatory physical interview at the bank's premises in Luxembourg for the director or an authorized signatory; remote-only onboarding will not be accepted if the beneficial ownership chain involves opaque jurisdictions or if the Belarusian/Russian? — generally, if UBO is from a high-risk country, physical presence is required. A Luxembourg-based professional co-creator may be accepted with a notarized power of attorney if the bank's compliance committee approves the file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low capital base and early-stage operation of the SARL with a new commercial profile in a non-licensed manufacturing/trading activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarized articles of association, proof of initial share capital deposit of EUR 12,000, a certified UBO register extract from the Luxembourg Register of Commercial and Companies (RCS), the business plan describing the enamel pin manufacturing supply chain, the signed contract with the Chinese/OEM producer, and pro-forma invoices from the supplier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border online marketplace sales via Etsy and Stripe creating a high volume of low-value third-party payments from individual buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Stripe merchant verification report, a sample of 10 Etsy transaction receipts, the Etsy account statement, the IP licensing/merchandise agreement if any, and a data-backed explanation of the average ticket size, refund rates, and dispute history to demonstrate a standard low-risk direct-to-consumer retail pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign directors and non-resident UBOs without a local tax or physical footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified passport copies, proof of address (utility bill, bank statement), a professional reference letter from the home-country bank, CVs of the directors, a declaration of non-appointment as PEP or sanctioned individual, a signed Luxembourg tax residence declaration, and a letter appointing a Luxembourg-based compliance agent if requested by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade settlement flows routed to China, Hong Kong, or other overseas manufacturing counterparties for physical goods purchases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Disclose the complete supplier onboarding package including the supplier's business registration certificate, bank account details, proforma invoice, bill of lading or shipping order, customs declaration, proof of payment instruction, and a distribution agreement clearly showing the arm's-length price for the die-struck brass blank and pin production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected future injection of shareholder loans or capital increases to fund inventory expansion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare shareholders' resolutions, board minutes approving the capital increase, the bank reference from the remitting bank, the loan agreement with interest rate and maturity terms if applicable, and the funding justification showing that the funds derive from the shareholders' savings or external financing and not from undisclosed third parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be executed via SWIFT international wire transfer in EUR to the SARL's Luxembourg capital escrow account. The remitting bank should use a coherent purpose-of-payment code; for an equity subscription from a shareholder, the purpose code 'S110 - Receipts from capital participation in a resident company' or the commonly used 'Equity Capital Contribution' in the SWIFT MT103 field 70 is accepted, while the BCL statistical report may treat it as a direct investment inflow. The receiving bank wil verify the UBO match against the RCS filing, the articles of association, the notarized subscription certificate, and the board resolution. All inbound capital contributions must be lodged through a bank holding a Luxembourg banking license or a recognized European authorized credit institution; a third-party payment platform cannot be used for statutory capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments to overseas suppliers and logistics providers must be cleared through SWIFT MT103 single payment instructions for the exact settlement amount, supported by the purchase order, proforma invoice, and contract. For bulk inventory purchases from China or other Asian suppliers, the SARL may use a documentary irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the Luxembourg bank in favor of the supplier's beneficiary bank, with the Bill of Lading and inspection certificate as required documents. Smaller operational payments such as courier fees, customs duties, and raw-material purchases may be made through SEPA Instant Credit Transfer within the eurozone or via MT103 to non-EU counterparties. The bank's sanction-screening and AML checks will apply to every outbound payment, but no foreign exchange license or separate central bank approval is required because Luxembourg maintains full capital movement freedom.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with a Luxembourg licensed bank
Foreign exchange swaps (FX swaps) for short-term working capital liquidity management
Standard currency options (European-style EUR/USD put/call) for selective trade-flow protection
Cross-currency swaps for long-term shareholder loans if the SARL later raises cross-currency debt

The SARL may enter into non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only as a concessionary measure for currencies with non-convertible local markets; NDFs have no practical regulatory benefit in the euro area and are not a preferred hedging instrument

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation (confirmation annuelle) reconfirming registered office, managers, constitutional documents and business activity data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; reference data as at 1 January of the filing year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines apply for late filing; good-standing certificates are withheld; persistent failure for two consecutive years enables the Public Prosecutor to seek judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (comptes annuels) together with management report and audit report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) in the framework of the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the balance-sheet date; a SARL closing on 31 December must file by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors face fines and civil liability; the LBR may reject incomplete deposits and the Public Prosecutor may pursue judicial strike-off (radiation) after repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) including the effect of any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmed annually together with the RCS confirmation by 31 March; share transfers and UBO changes must be reported within 30 days of the event under the Law of 13 January 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines between EUR 1,250 and EUR 1,250,000 for the entity; criminal sanctions for deliberately false declarations; persistent default may lead to RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) and municipal business tax (IBC) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 May of the year following the calendar tax year; ACD routinely grants extension to 31 October on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office) with 10% administrative surcharge; automatic late-payment interest at 9.5% p.a.; no tax residency certificate issued until returns are cleared.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) annual return and payment of the minimum tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual CIT return by 31 May (extension to 31 October); minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 for small balance sheets under EUR 350,000, otherwise EUR 1,000, payable in full
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Enforced collection with statutory preferential claim; late-payment interest at 9.5% p.a.; the minimum tax cannot be waived in loss-making years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A state-approved independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is compulsory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4M, net turnover EUR 8.8M, average headcount 50; micro and small SARLs below these thresholds are exempt from statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Law of 19 December 2002 as amended (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is optional for non-listed companies and mandatory for public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must reconfirm its beneficial-owner file in the RBE each year during the RCS annual confirmation window (1 January-31 March); any share transfer or change in the control chain must be declared to the RBE within 30 days of the event; the on-site UBO register must always mirror the exact current shareholding structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger recording all SARL part transfers)
Register of Beneficial Owners (on-site counterpart of the RBE under the Law of 13 January 2019)
Minute Book of shareholders' and managers' meetings
Accounting records, invoices and supporting documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 1,650-3,850 per year (EUR 1,500-3,500) covering registered office/domiciliation and corporate secretarial services in the Luxembourg market
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 5,500-16,500 per year (EUR 5,000-15,000) for a full Luxembourg statutory audit; not incurred while the SARL qualifies for the small-company audit exemption

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate rate for a limited liability company in Luxembourg City, comprising 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and 6.75% municipal business tax; lower 22.80% aggregate rate applies to taxable income below EUR 175,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays for manufacturing of hard enamel lapel pins. Available preferential incentives: R&D tax credit for qualified research expenses (up to 25% credit base), tax credit for capital investment, notional interest deduction on new equity, and the IP Box regime (80% exemption on net qualifying IP income).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via MyGuichet (www.guichet.lu) by the company's tax representative or legal representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g., by 31 May for a 31 December year-end); extensions may be granted for up to seven months upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit or loss before taxes, as reported in the annual statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident SARL reports worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders are not required to file a separate return for the company's income; only the company files this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions for non-deductible expenses (e.g., fines, gifts, 50% of entertainment expenses, expenses not at arm's length).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any interest or royalty paid to non-resident affiliates above an arm's length amount; apply the Luxembourg thin-capitalization or EBDTA limitation if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for tax-exempt income (e.g., 50% exemption on qualifying dividend income, IP Box exemption, and other legal exemptions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company holds a non-resident subsidiary or earns foreign royalties, attach the relevant ownership and substance evidence to support the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from previous years available to offset the current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a Luxembourg resident company cannot be transferred to foreign affiliates or shareholders; carryforward period is 17 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after dividends, interest, lease rent (if any), and loss-offset; base for the corporate income tax and municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a resident SARL, all declared amounts are taxable; the same taxable base is used for CIT and municipal business tax assessed by the commune.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty of 10% of the assessed tax due if the return is filed within two months after the deadline, increasing to 20% thereafter. Interest on unpaid tax accrues at 0.6% per month. Additional administrative fines up to EUR 2,500 may be imposed, and the tax authority may assess taxes ex officio.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower dividend withholding rate under an applicable DTA, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide an official residence certificate (Tax Residence Certificate) issued by the foreign competent authority before the dividend payment date. The withholding agent must submit Form 62 (application for withholding tax reduction) to the Luxembourg tax administration. If the shareholder is an EU/EEA company holding at least a 10% participation for a continuous 12-month period, the 0% Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies via procedure Form 271.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory rate; reduced to 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive and to 5-10% under most DTA protocols. Interest: 0% statutory withholding tax (Luxembourg generally does not levy WHT on interest unless anti-abuse rules apply to payments made to certain low-tax jurisdictions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: required when the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; Local File: required where the total related-party cross-border transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per fiscal year. Thresholds are applied in euros, and currency conversion is made at the applicable ECB rate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulations as in the UAE, the tax authorities require genuine substance (adequate physical premises, employed staff, and management oversight) for the SARL to be recognized as resident and to access treaty/EU directive benefits. Purely artificial or letterbox arrangements linked to enamel pin manufacturing are challenged through general anti-abuse rules (GAAR) and the OECD Principal Purpose Test (PPT).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating sales of hard enamel lapel pins on Etsy or Stripe, maintaining a second accounting record, destroying purchase invoices, or hiding taxable profits in personal accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction for tax evasion: imprisonment of liable individuals for up to 5 years and/or a fine up to EUR 250,000 or double the evaded tax. Administrative surcharge of up to 20% of the under-declared corporate income tax plus monthly late interest at 0.6%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent or reckless conduct; directors face civil restitution of the unpaid tax, potential travel bans, disqualification from management for a period of 10 years, and imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Luxembourg SARL as a shell intermediary for invoicing pin sales without exercising any genuine manufacturing, purchasing, or distribution activity; centralized accounting and of correspondence only.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the PPT clause and loss of Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption; the tax authority may re-characterize the income and impose additional corporate income tax and municipal business tax of up to 24.94%, plus an administrative penalty of 10% on the reassessed amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly operate the shell structure become jointly and severally liable for the tax deficit, may be personally assessed on the profits, and can be barred from serving as directors in Luxembourg for a period of 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting anonymous or suspicious payments via Etsy Direct Pay or Stripe without performing basic customer due diligence or failing to maintain transaction records; knowingly processing funds or proceeds from corruption or other serious crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended): for legal persons, fines up to EUR 1 million; administrative fines up to EUR 1 million imposed by the Luxembourg supervisory authority. Additionally, the court may order closure of the business premises or confiscation of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face imprisonment for up to 5 years and personal fines up to EUR 250,000; severe breaches trigger travel bans, asset freezes, and personal liability if the company was insolvent and the director acted in bad faith.
